title: Southbound Logistics — field capture and integration scratchbook
content:
Context: quick personal capture from 2025-09-16 call with Southbound Logistics (SBL). They are evaluating a Private deployment (VPC) for an internal dispatch/assistant use case — medium size (50–70 agents), intermittent burst loads from mobile apps + web dashboard, strict P95 latency reqs for interactive routing edits (P95 < 200ms target), and regulatory requirement to keep PII inside their VPC. This is a working scratchpad — messy, prioritized to-dos and open questions for follow-up with SBL AE + infra team.

Attendees (call):
- Eileen Park (SBL product)
- Omar Rahman (SBL infra)
- Lydia Chen (SBL data/ops)
- Maya Chen (Redwood SE)
- Diego Alvarez (Redwood infra SME)

High level ask / desired end state:
- Private deployment inside SBL AWS account (we call it Private/VPC) with customer-managed subnets and KMS integration.
- Serve two models: a smaller 7B assistant for routing edits and a 13B fluent summarizer for post-trip summaries.
- Guarantee 95th percentile latency for edit flows < 200ms under steady state 200 rps, spiky to 800 rps for short windows (2–5m).
- Audit logs and retention for 90 days, with ability to stream to SBL Splunk.
- Automatic fallback to hosted Redwood model if local capacity saturated is acceptable only if customer approves network egress policy — likely not allowed for PII.

Initial notes / gotchas (operational + infra):
- VPC peering vs PrivateLink: SBL prefers PrivateLink for tighter control; we need to validate our Private control plane compatibility and NAT gateway requirements.
- KMS/HSM: they use AWS KMS; ask: do they have an external HSM requirement? (Omar: not at first, may be later).
- Egress policy: legal likely to forbid any outbound model fallback. Means we must size Dedicated pool to handle 99.9% of traffic.
- Load spikes: 800 rps spike would require autoscale/burst capacity plan. Need to model token cost and GPU footprint for both models under expected per-request token distribution.
- Tokenization mismatch: SBL's payloads include long protobuf-encoded trip histories (up to ~6k tokens). Ask: do they want truncation, semantic chunking, or streaming with a windowed KV cache?
- Caching opportunities: user-level prefix cache for repeated agent prompts looks promising — could cut cost by ~30% on routing-edit paths. Need to propose cache-key schema.
- Quantization: customer wants to run 13B with int4 if possible; we need to confirm quality regression tolerance metrics and propose test prompts for redline.
- GPU selection: infer32-bit baseline on A10G-like or prefer A100s? Diego: A10G equivalent is cheaper but may struggle on long-sequence with 13B int4; recommend mixed fleet and autoscale policies.

SLO / performance modeling (rough):
- Edit flow (7B): median tokens 120, p95 tokens 420. Target 200ms p95 => must keep batching low (<=2) and prioritize single-request lanes. Suggest dedicated low-latency pool with 1–2 replicas per AZ.
- Summary flow (13B): median tokens 900, p95 tokens 2400. Higher throughput tolerant (p95 <= 2s). Can be routed to separate capacity tier with aggressive batching to reduce cost.
- Failover constraints: since no egress allowed, build intra-VPC fallback to smaller cached model variant + degraded feature flag for UI to indicate slow path.

Security / compliance points:
- Audit log forwarding to Splunk via Kinesis or S3 sink — ensure we support encryption at rest and correct IAM role setup.
- Data retention: 90 days; need to confirm which logs include PII and whether PII must be redacted before retention.
- Pen test / SOC: they asked about SOC2 plus penetration test windows. Prep checklist: provide SOC2 report, discuss pen test schedule, include contact in security team.

Prompting / quality considerations:
- Routing-edit prompts rely on precise step-by-step state deltas; we must avoid hallucination for coordinates and ETA. Propose guardrails: structured-output schema + deterministic reranker (embedding similarity) to validate candidate route changes.
- Suggest building prompt/eval suite: 200 seed prompts from real logs (redacted) + 50 adversarial cases. We need SBL to grant sample dataset (redacted) for quality eval.

Immediate action items (owner / date):
- Diego: produce rough capacity estimate (GPU types, counts, expected cost) for steady 200 rps + 3x burst to 800 rps, include warmup times — due 2025-09-22.
- Maya: draft integration note for Private deployment network diagram (customer VPC, subnets, endpoints, route tables, KMS) + questions list for Omar — due 2025-09-19. (IN PROGRESS)
- Priya: assemble evaluation prompt set template and quality metrics sheet; propose production acceptance criteria for quantization runs — due 2025-09-24.
- Lydia (SBL): provide 3 redacted example records (routing edit, full trip summary, edge-case long trip) and confirm retention policy details — requested 2025-09-19.
- Diego/Maya: schedule on-site/remote arch review with SBL infra next week; propose two 90-minute sessions (network + runtime) — propose dates.

Open questions to resolve (prioritized):
1) Egress policy final sign-off from legal — if egress allowed for non-PII fallback, we can save ~30% in cost by leveraging hosted failover. (HIGH)
2) HSM requirement later in roadmap — may shift key management design. (MED)
3) Exact token distribution for summary requests — need sample histogram to model batching impact. (HIGH)
4) Acceptance criteria for int4 quantization quality — what BLEU/ROUGE/label-accuracy thresholds do they accept? (MED)

Notes for proposal draft:
- Two-pool architecture: low-latency 7B pool (no batching, reserved capacity) + high-throughput 13B pool (batched, autoscaled). Express cost tradeoffs and SLA targets per route.
- Offer a three-month private POC: initial load testing + quantization evaluation + implement audit forwarding; milestones at 2 weeks (network/infra review), 6 weeks (load test + quality baseline), 12 weeks (rollout + handoff).
- Pricing: give ballpark for reserved capacity monthly + one-time integration support fee. Include optional managed observability add-on for extended retention beyond 90 days.

Slack shorthand / fragments captured during call (raw):
"if egress is blocked, we need 3x buffer for spikes"
"routing-edit mustn't batch >2 or UX will stutter"
"can we run a tiny embedding reranker local for correctness check?"
"they use protobuf blobs — need ingestion parser to extract text windows"

Risks and mitigations quick list:
- Risk: underestimated burst capacity -> mitigation: implement surge queue with graceful degraded UI + request throttling and pre-warm schedules for peak windows.
- Risk: quantization breaks critical fields -> mitigation: A/B test with labeled correctness set, roll back to fp16 if delta > threshold.
- Risk: legal blocks outbound fallback -> mitigation: design 2-tier within-VPC fallback and clear cost estimates.

Next meeting: schedule follow-up with Omar + Lydia first week of 2025-09-22. Agenda: share Diego capacity estimate, confirm egress/legal stance, review redacted sample records.

Misc notes to self: capture sample prompt templates, ask SBL for response latency expectations per geographic region (they have multiple regions in us-east-1 and eu-west-1), include cost-per-token estimate per model variant in proposal.

-- end scratchbook --
